EN_MODERN.text: Yahweh’s anger burned against Uzzah; and God struck him there for his error; and he died there by God’s ark.
EN_MODERN.commentary: This chapter describes King David’s effort to bring the Ark of the Covenant to Jerusalem, an event that begins with joyful celebration but turns tragic during transport. In this specific verse, Uzzah is struck down for touching the sacred ark in violation of strict religious protocols regarding its handling.

EN_MODERN.text: Saul said, I will give her to him, that she may be a snare to him, and that the hand of the Philistines may be against him. Therefore Saul said to David, “You shall today be my son-in-law a second time.”
EN_MODERN.commentary: Chapter 18 details the growing military success of David, which earns him the adoration of the people and the deep paranoia and jealousy of King Saul. In this verse, Saul schemes to use the marriage of his daughter Michal as a trap to endanger David's life through the Philistines while publicly offering him royal kinship.

EN_MODERN.text: if the anointed priest sins so as to bring guilt on the people, then let him offer for his sin, which he has sinned, a young bull without defect to Yahweh for a sin offering.
EN_MODERN.commentary: This chapter of Leviticus outlines the legal and ritual procedures for the purification (or "sin") offerings required when individuals commit unintentional violations of divine commandments. Within this context, the verse specifies that if the high priest—who represents the spiritual well-being of the entire community—commits an inadvertent sin, he must offer a flawless young bull to restore ritual purity and avert communal guilt.

EN_OLD.text:
If I wait, the grave
is mine house: I have made my bed in the darkness.
EN_OLD.commentary: Chapter 17 of the Book of Job continues Job's response to his friends, during which he laments his worsening physical condition, mocks their inability to understand his situation, and expresses his despair over his imminent death. Within this context of profound physical suffering and hopelessness, the verse reflects Job’s resignation to his fate, viewing the grave as his only remaining dwelling place and rest.

EN_OLD.text: And he led them on safely, so that they feared not: but the sea overwhelmed their enemies.
EN_OLD.commentary: Psalm 78 is a historical psalm that recounts God's deliverance of the Israelites from Egypt and their subsequent wanderings in the wilderness despite their frequent rebellions. Within this narrative, this verse specifically recalls the parting of the Red Sea, highlighting how God safely guided the Israelites across while drowning their Egyptian pursuers.

EN_OLD.text: I rejoiced greatly that I found of thy children walking in truth, as we have received a commandment from the Father.
EN_OLD.commentary:
**Chapter Context**
The second Epistle of John is a brief letter addressed from "the elder" to a specific Christian community (referred to as the "elect lady and her children"). The letter warns against false teachers who deny the incarnation of Jesus and emphasizes the foundational commandments of love and truth.

**Verse Context**
In this verse, the author expresses his happiness upon learning that some members of the community are adhering to Christian teachings and moral standards. This statement serves as an encouraging opening that sets a positive tone before the letter's subsequent warnings against deception.

NL_OLD.text: De zonen van Merari: Maheli, zijn zoon, Libni, zijn zoon, Shimei, zijn zoon, Uzza, zijn zoon,
NL_OLD.commentary: Dit hoofdstuk geeft een gedetailleerd overzicht van de genealogie van de Levieten, de stam die verantwoordelijk was voor de tabernakel- en tempeldienst, met specifieke aandacht voor de afstammelingen van Aäron en de andere Levietische families. Dit vers maakt deel uit van de geslachtslijst van de familie van Merari, een van de drie hoofdgroepen van de Levieten.

NL_MODERN.text: Zij zagen de God van Israel. Onder zijn voeten was het alsof er een vloer van saffier lag, zo helder als de hemel zelf.
NL_MODERN.commentary: In Exodus 24 sluit Mozes namens het volk Israël een officieel verbond met God bij de berg Sinaï, waarna de oudsten van Israël naar de berg mogen op klimmen. In dit specifieke vers wordt hun visioen van God beschreven, waarbij Zijn aanwezigheid wordt verbeeld als stralend en hemels.

NL_MODERN.text: In die tijd was Debora, een profetes die getrouwd was met Lappidot, de lechteres van Israël.
NL_MODERN.commentary: Richteren 4 beschrijft de periode waarin het volk Israël wordt onderdrukt door de Kanaänitische koning Jabin, en hoe de profetes Debora en de legersteun van Barak leiden tot een bevrijdende overwinning. Dit vers introduceert Debora feitelijk als de politieke leider en rechter van Israël te midden van deze crisis, wat haar unieke gezag en centrale rol in de komende gebeurtenissen vestigt.
